Foundations of American Democracy: Natural rights
Locke's idea that life, liberty, and property precede government
Popular sovereignty
The principle that governmental authority comes from the people
Social contract
The agreement in which people surrender some freedom for protection
Republicanism
Government by elected representatives rather than direct rule
Participatory democracy
A model emphasising broad, direct citizen involvement
Pluralist democracy
A model where organised interest groups compete for influence
Elite democracy
A model where a small group of educated people makes decisions
Articles of Confederation
The first national framework, with a weak central government
Shays' Rebellion
The uprising that exposed the weakness of the Articles
Great Compromise
The deal creating a House by population and a Senate by equal state votes
Three-Fifths Compromise
Counting three of every five enslaved people for representation
Federalist No. 10
Madison's argument that a large republic controls the effects of faction
Federalist No. 51
Madison's argument for separation of powers and checks and balances
Brutus No. 1
The Anti-Federalist warning that a large republic threatens liberty
Federalism
The division of power between national and state governments
Enumerated powers
Powers explicitly granted to the national government
Reserved powers
Powers left to the states under the Tenth Amendment
Concurrent powers
Powers shared by both national and state governments
Necessary and proper clause
The provision allowing Congress to enact laws to execute its powers
Commerce clause
The provision giving Congress authority over interstate commerce
McCulloch v. Maryland
The ruling upholding implied powers and national supremacy
United States v. Lopez
The ruling limiting the commerce clause by striking a gun-free zone law
Categorical grant
Federal money given for a narrow purpose with strict conditions
Block grant
Federal money given for a broad purpose with state discretion
Unfunded mandate
A federal requirement imposed on states without funding
Interactions Among Branches of Governmen: The division of the legislature into two chambers
Powers listed in Article I, Section 8
Extended Senate debate used to block a vote
The Senate procedure ending a filibuster with sixty votes
A House procedure forcing a bill out of committee
A House procedure easing debate rules on legislation
The House committee controlling debate terms for bills
A temporary joint committee reconciling House and Senate versions
Funding directed to a member's district for local benefit
Trading votes to secure passage of each member's priority
Drawing district lines to favour a party or group
The ruling opening redistricting to judicial review and one person one vote
The ruling that race cannot be the predominant factor in drawing districts
Spending required by law versus set annually by appropriation
Powers explicitly listed, such as veto and commander in chief
Powers such as executive orders and the bully pulpit
A bill dying when the president does not sign it near a session's end
An international deal made without Senate ratification
A presidential comment on how a law will be interpreted
The constitutional address that sets a legislative agenda
The power of courts to strike down unconstitutional actions
The principle of deciding cases according to precedent
Willingness to overturn precedent versus deference to elected branches
Agency latitude in interpreting and applying law
The alliance of an agency, a committee, and an interest group
Congressional monitoring of executive branch performance
Civil Liberties and Civil Rights: Civil liberties
Protections from government action, largely in the Bill of Rights
Civil rights
Protections against discrimination guaranteeing equal treatment
Selective incorporation
Applying Bill of Rights protections to states through the Fourteenth Amendment
Establishment clause
The prohibition on government establishing religion
Free exercise clause
The protection of religious practice from government interference
Engel v. Vitale
The ruling that state-sponsored school prayer violates establishment
Wisconsin v. Yoder
The ruling protecting Amish free exercise against compulsory schooling
Schenck v. United States
The ruling that speech creating a clear and present danger is unprotected
Tinker v. Des Moines
The ruling protecting symbolic student speech that does not disrupt school
New York Times v. United States
The ruling against prior restraint in the Pentagon Papers case
Symbolic speech
Expressive conduct protected under the First Amendment
Prior restraint
Government censorship before publication, presumed unconstitutional
Libel and slander
Unprotected false statements harming reputation in writing or speech
McDonald v. Chicago
The ruling incorporating the Second Amendment against the states
Exclusionary rule
Barring illegally obtained evidence from trial
Miranda v. Arizona
The ruling requiring warning of rights before custodial interrogation
Gideon v. Wainwright
The ruling requiring counsel for felony defendants who cannot pay
Due process clause
The guarantee of fair procedures before deprivation of liberty
Roe v. Wade
The ruling recognising a privacy-based abortion right in 1973
Brown v. Board of Education
The ruling that segregated public schools are unconstitutional
Equal protection clause
The Fourteenth Amendment guarantee of equal treatment under law
Letter from Birmingham Jail
King's defence of nonviolent direct action against unjust laws
Civil Rights Act of 1964
The law banning discrimination in public accommodations and employment
Voting Rights Act of 1965
The law eliminating barriers to Black voter registration
Affirmative action
Policies considering group status to remedy past discrimination
Title IX
The law prohibiting sex discrimination in federally funded education
American Political Ideologies and Belief: Political socialization
The process by which people acquire political beliefs
Agents of political socialization
Family, school, peers, media, and major events
Generational effect
Shared events shaping the politics of an entire age cohort
Political ideology
A coherent set of beliefs about government's proper role
Liberal ideology
Support for government action on economic equality and social freedom
Conservative ideology
Support for limited economic regulation and traditional social values
Libertarian ideology
Support for minimal government in both economic and social life
Public opinion poll
A survey measuring attitudes in a population
Random sampling
Selecting respondents so each has an equal chance of inclusion
Sampling error
The margin of uncertainty in a poll's estimate
Benchmark poll
An early poll establishing baseline support for a candidate
Exit poll
A survey of voters immediately after they cast ballots
Tracking poll
Repeated polling showing change in opinion over time
Question wording bias
Phrasing that pushes respondents toward a particular answer
Political efficacy
The belief that one's participation can affect government
Keynesian economics in policy
Using government spending to manage demand
Supply-side economics in policy
Cutting taxes and regulation to spur production
Party realignment
A durable shift in the coalitions supporting each party
Political Participation: Suffrage
The legal right to vote
Fifteenth Amendment
The amendment prohibiting denial of the vote based on race
Nineteenth Amendment
The amendment granting women the right to vote
Twenty-Sixth Amendment
The amendment lowering the voting age to eighteen
Voter turnout
The share of eligible citizens who actually vote
Rational choice voting
Voting based on what is judged to be in one's own interest
Retrospective voting
Voting based on evaluation of an incumbent's record
Prospective voting
Voting based on what a candidate promises to do
Party-line voting
Supporting all candidates of one party on a ballot
Political party functions
Recruiting candidates, mobilising voters, and organising government
Party platform
The official statement of a party's positions
Winner-take-all system
An electoral rule awarding everything to the plurality winner
Duverger's law
The tendency of single-member districts to produce two parties
Third party role
Raising issues that major parties later adopt
Closed versus open primary
A primary limited to registered party members versus open to all
Caucus
A meeting where party members select a nominee through discussion
Electoral College
The body of electors that formally elects the president
Interest group
An organisation seeking to influence public policy
Lobbying
Direct communication with officials to influence decisions
Political action committee
An organisation that raises and spends money for candidates
Citizens United v. FEC
The ruling that independent political spending is protected speech
Free rider problem in interest groups
People benefiting from group efforts without joining
Social movement
Broad collective action pressing for political change
Linkage institution
A channel such as media or parties connecting people to government
Horse-race journalism
Media coverage focused on who is winning rather than on policy
